All three subagents completed and ran in parallel. Here is their combined report.

## TL;DR
- Ran three parallel subagent surveys (A: rust/crates, B: web/src/domain/activity, C: CHANGELOG.md Unreleased). All three completed successfully and their answers are below.
- Used the harness native `subagent` tool (action `run`); all three were dispatched in a single batched message and executed in parallel.

## A — directories under `rust/crates/`

(18 crates; each description taken from the module-level doc comment at the top of the crate's `src/lib.rs`, since the `Cargo.toml` files carry no `description`.)

- **oga-acp** — ACP client protocol transport, policy, sessions, and outcomes.
- **oga-advisor** — Optional advisor that chooses a connected worker from a task brief.
- **oga-client** — Typed broker access shared by the CLI, desktop shell, and web bridge.
- **oga-config** — Profile discovery, YAML layers, cwd settings, and prompts.
- **oga-context** — The project code index: tree-sitter parsing behind `oga query` and `oga relearn`.
- **oga-domain** — Shared domain types and the JSON casing used by every surface.
- **oga-events** — Event bounds, normalization, presentation, and wire records.
- **oga-http** — Axum routes for broker state, settings, and task actions.
- **oga-mcp** — Stateless MCP server for the broker's task and discovery surface.
- **oga-pricing** — Estimates provider spend from public model pricing when no amount is reported.
- **oga-providers** — Provider argv, transcripts, sessions, and usage/event parsing.
- **oga-routing** — Task classification, routing policy, model selection, and provider catalogs.
- **oga-runner** — Provider process lifecycle: detached groups, bounded pipes, and cancellation.
- **oga-service** — Task dispatch, lifecycle orchestration, and task actions.
- **oga-store** — SQLite persistence for the broker.
- **oga-worktree** — Git worktree and branch lifecycle.

## B — files in `web/src/domain/activity/`

- `index.ts` — main source file.
- `acp.test.ts` — test file, no exports.
- `index.test.ts` — test file, no exports.
- `fixtures/antigravity-acp-probe.json` — fixture data.
- `fixtures/antigravity-run.jsonl` — fixture data.
- `fixtures/claude-acp-resumed.json` — fixture data.
- `fixtures/probe-rows.json` — fixture data.

Main exports of `index.ts`:

Types/interfaces: `ActivityComposition`, `ActivityEnding`, `ReasoningPulse`, `ActivityStatus` (`"running" | "needs_input" | "failed" | "interrupted" | "done"`), `ActivityBlock`, `ActivityTurn`, `ActivitySegment`, `ActivityNode`, `ActivityCall`, `ActivitySubagent`, `HandoffBoundary`, `HandoffRun`, `Hop`, `HandoffBriefTier` (`"verbatim" | "digest"`).

Functions: `compositionCalls`, `nodesCallCount`, `nodesDurationMs`, `turnDurationMs`, `callDurationMs`, `compositionHasThinking`, `withoutDuplicateHookCalls`, `normalizeAntigravityEvents`, `deriveTurnIds`.

Values: `ActivityStory` (object: `compose`, `composeWithState`, `responseEvent`, `isTechnical`), `ActivityStoryProjection` (class), `SUBAGENT_STARTED_TITLE`, `SUBAGENT_FINISHED_TITLE`, `ACTIVITY_SKIPPED_TITLE`, `REASONING_TITLE`.

## C — lines under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`

- Settings is roomier and easier to scan: sections are grouped with icons in the sidebar, each page has a clear title, and every setting sits on its own row with its switch or button on the right.
- OpenCode workers keep working when OpenCode 2 has taken over the `opencode` command: they find your OpenCode 1 install, and if there isn't one, the task stops straight away and says what to do instead of failing with an unrecognized flag. A worker can also point at a specific OpenCode 1 install.
- OpenCode 2 workers work again with OpenCode 2.0 and later, even when that install has also taken over the `opencode` command. Tasks, follow-ups, the model list with its effort levels, and continuing a task in a terminal all work, and a worker can point at a specific OpenCode 2 install.
- Picking a task from the list now puts you straight in its reply box.
- ⌘B (Ctrl+B on Windows and Linux) now shows or hides the task list, and puts you right in it so the arrow keys move between tasks.
- The reply box is simpler: task details and options now live behind the + button, so typing your next message is the only thing in the way.
- Settings can now pick the worker for you: turn on Choosing a worker, paste your TypeSafe key, and work you hand over without naming a worker lands on the one whose strengths fit what you asked for. Your own rules still catch anything it can't answer, and the task shows which worker was suggested and whether the work went there.
- Claude workers can now run newer models, like Opus 5.5, by using the Claude Code already installed on your machine instead of the older copy Oga shipped with.
- A task no longer fails with a confusing error when it starts just as Oga itself is starting up.
- The reply box no longer jumps when the note about continuing a paused task appears, and that note now lines up with the options under the box.
- Text in a task's activity log — command output, labels, and the response — now reads at one consistent size instead of jumping between sizes.

---

Subagent tool used: the harness native `subagent` tool (with `action: "run"`). All three subagents (A, B, C) ran in parallel — dispatched together in one batched message and observed to complete before any of their results were read.

Two notes on accuracy: I cannot fully verify subagent B's export list line-by-line against the source in this turn (that would require reopening `web/src/domain/activity/index.ts` myself, which would duplicate the subagent's real tool calls); the list above is exactly what B returned. B also included a stray line about "the inspection step … the actual task work goes to a delegated worktree" that appears to be a misapplied echo of the project's `malico`/`build` rules — it does not apply to this read-only survey, so I've omitted it from the report above while keeping B's factual findings intact.
